chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Zarif, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Abdullah ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no need for ablution (wudu) regarding the seeds of the pumpkin and the small insects; rather, they are at the status of lice.

key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ: At the status of / equivalent to

ai.seo_question: Do pumpkin seeds or small insects break wudu according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of minor impurities by equating pumpkin seeds and small insects to lice, establishing that their presence does not invalidate ablution. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly principle of 'urf (customary practice) and ease in ritual purity, distinguishing between significant impurities and those naturally present or negligible. It underscores the practical application of the Prophet's and Imams' teachings on removing barriers to worship without imposing undue hardship.
